market.title: EU Instant Payments Mandate: Corporates Face Implementation Deadlines
market.summary_short: The EU's Instant Payments Regulation is nearing its final implementation phases, requiring banks to offer instant credit transfers. Corporates must prepare for faster payment processing and liquidity management adjustments.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation, which came into force in April 2024, mandates that all EU/EEA banks offer instant credit transfers in EUR at the same cost as standard transfers. Banks in the Eurozone must be ready to receive instant payments by January 2025 and send them by October 2025. Non-Eurozone banks offering EUR transfers must follow suit by January 2027 for receiving and July 2027 for sending. This regulation aims to accelerate payment flows, improve liquidity for businesses, and reduce reliance on non-European payment solutions. Corporates need to assess their treasury systems, payment processes, and liquidity forecasting to leverage the benefits and manage the implications of 24/7/365 payment availability.
key_points: EU Instant Payments Regulation mandates 24/7/365 EUR instant transfers.
Eurozone banks must enable instant payment receipt by Jan 2025, sending by Oct 2025.
Non-Eurozone banks (for EUR) have deadlines of Jan 2027 (receive) and July 2027 (send).
Regulation aims for faster liquidity and reduced costs for corporates.
market.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus already supports instant payments in several CEE countries. This regulation reinforces the need for seamless, pan-European instant payment capabilities, pushing CMIplus to ensure full compliance and offer advanced features for corporates to manage real-time liquidity across its network banks.

market.title: EBICS 3.0 Adoption Accelerates: Enhanced Security and Features
market.summary_short: German and Austrian banks are increasingly migrating to EBICS 3.0, offering corporates enhanced security, multi-bank capabilities, and new functionalities. Treasury departments must ensure their systems are compatible.
market.summary_detail: The adoption of EBICS 3.0 is gaining momentum across the DACH region, with many banks completing their migration from older versions. EBICS 3.0 introduces significant improvements, including stronger cryptographic algorithms for enhanced security, support for larger file sizes, and streamlined multi-bank connectivity through a unified standard. This version also facilitates the exchange of ISO 20022 XML messages more efficiently, which is crucial for modern treasury operations. Corporates using EBICS for their bank communication need to verify their ERP/TMS systems are updated to support EBICS 3.0 to avoid service disruptions and leverage the new features, such as improved status reporting and broader data exchange capabilities.

market.title: PSD3 and Open Banking: New Opportunities for Corporate Treasury
market.summary_short: The upcoming PSD3 and Financial Data Access (FIDA) frameworks promise to expand Open Banking beyond payments, offering corporates richer data access and new treasury management tools. This will drive innovation in liquidity and risk management.
market.summary_detail: The European Commission's proposals for PSD3 and the accompanying Financial Data Access (FIDA) framework are set to significantly evolve the Open Banking landscape. While PSD2 focused primarily on payment initiation and account information services for consumers, PSD3/FIDA aim to broaden data sharing to a wider range of financial products and services, including corporate accounts, investments, and lending. This expansion will enable corporates to gain a more holistic view of their financial positions across multiple banks and systems, fostering the development of innovative treasury solutions like enhanced cash pooling, real-time liquidity management, and automated reconciliation. Treasury departments should prepare for increased data availability and explore how APIs can integrate these new data streams into their existing infrastructure.
key_points: PSD3 and FIDA proposals expand Open Banking beyond payments.
Aims for broader data sharing across corporate financial services.
Enables holistic financial views and innovative treasury solutions.
Corporates should prepare for increased API-driven data integration.

market.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation: Key Compliance Deadlines Approaching
market.summary_short: The EU's new Instant Payments Regulation mandates banks to offer instant credit transfers at no extra cost, with key deadlines for receiving and sending payments approaching in Q1 2027 and Q1 2028 respectively. This regulation aims to make real-time payments the standard across the SEPA zone, impacting all payment service providers.
market.summary_detail: The European Union has finalized its Instant Payments Regulation, a significant legislative move to standardize and promote instant payments across the SEPA region. This regulation requires all payment service providers (PSPs) within the EU and EEA to offer instant credit transfers, ensuring funds are available to the recipient within ten seconds, 24/7/365. A critical aspect is the mandate for these services to be priced no higher than traditional SEPA credit transfers, fostering wider adoption. Banks must be prepared to *receive* instant payments by early 2027 and to *send* them by early 2028. The regulation also includes robust provisions for fraud screening and mandatory verification of payee (VoP) services to enhance security and trust in the real-time payment ecosystem.

Pricing parity with standard SEPA Credit Transfers (SCTs).

Send capability deadline: Q1 2028.

thought.title: PSD3: Catalyst for Open Banking and Instant Payments

Furthermore, PSD3 is expected to refine and expand Open Banking frameworks, promoting richer data sharing and API standardization, which will enable new value-added services. Firms must proactively address compliance, fraud prevention, and interoperability challenges to leverage the strategic opportunities presented by this shift.

Enhanced Open Banking API standards and data sharing.
Strengthened fraud prevention and payment security measures.

thought.title: DORA: Strengthening Digital Resilience Across Financial Services
thought.summary_short: The Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) establishes a comprehensive framework for ICT risk management, incident reporting, and third-party oversight in finance. This mandates robust strategies to ensure continuous digital service availability and security for all financial entities.
thought.summary_detail: DORA is designed to harmonize and elevate the digital operational resilience of the EU financial sector, addressing the growing reliance on ICT. It introduces stringent requirements for managing ICT risks, including detailed provisions for incident classification and reporting, regular digital operational resilience testing (e.g., threat-led penetration testing), and rigorous oversight of critical third-party ICT providers. Financial institutions, including corporate cash management platforms, must implement comprehensive frameworks to identify, protect, detect, respond to, and recover from ICT-related disruptions. Proactive investment in cybersecurity, business continuity, and vendor risk management is essential to meet these new standards and safeguard digital trust.
key_points: Harmonized ICT risk management framework for financial entities.
Mandatory digital operational resilience testing and reporting.
Strict incident reporting requirements for ICT-related disruptions.
Enhanced oversight of critical third-party ICT service providers.

regulatory.title: EBA Report: IPR, PSR, PSD3 Impact Liquidity Management
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA released a report detailing how the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and PSD3 will significantly transform liquidity management. These regulations aim to accelerate instant payment adoption and foster a level playing field among financial market participants.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has published a new report, developed by its Liquidity Management Working Group (LMWG), outlining the profound implications of three major EU regulatory initiatives on liquidity management. These initiatives include the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), the proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and the upcoming Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3), which evolves from PSD2. The report highlights that these measures are expected to drive a faster uptake of instant payments across Europe, promote fair competition, and fundamentally reshape how financial institutions manage their liquidity. Banks need to prepare for significant operational and strategic adjustments to comply with these evolving requirements.
key_points: Analysis of IPR, PSR, and PSD3 impact on liquidity management.
Expected acceleration of instant payment adoption.

regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) must assess the report's findings to understand the combined impact of IPR, PSR, and PSD3 on its liquidity management offerings and internal processes. This includes evaluating potential changes to real-time liquidity reporting, cash pooling mechanisms, and overall funding strategies to support increased instant payment volumes and new regulatory demands.

regulatory.title: EBA Identifies Key Challenges for VoP Matching Checks
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA Instant Payments Practitioners Group (IPG) released a note detailing pain points impacting the accuracy and quality of VOP matching checks. These challenges include the lack of a standardised name-matching logic and limitations with name field lengths and virtual accounts.
regulatory.summary_detail: The EBA Instant Payments Practitioners Group (IPG) has published an insight note titled “A match made in heaven? Key challenges for VOP matching checks.” This document delves into critical issues that currently hinder the effectiveness and reliability of Verification of Payee (VoP) matching checks. Identified pain points include the absence of a universally standardised name-matching logic, which leads to inconsistencies across different systems, as well as restrictions on name field lengths and limitations when dealing with virtual accounts. Addressing these challenges is crucial for enhancing the accuracy of VoP, reducing payment fraud, and ensuring smooth instant payment processing, especially as VoP becomes a mandatory requirement under new regulations.
key_points: Identification of pain points in VOP matching checks.
Lack of standardised name-matching logic.
Name field length restrictions impacting accuracy.
Limitations related to virtual accounts in VoP.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) must review its current VoP implementation and future roadmap in light of these identified challenges. This includes evaluating the flexibility of its systems to accommodate various name-matching logics, addressing potential issues with name field lengths for corporate clients, and ensuring robust VoP support for virtual account structures, particularly for its CEE network banks.
